text: "My birds say Seat-03 still clutches a stone too smooth to be chance. They also whisper that Seat-06's nightingale hums the same tune as Seat-01's lullaby. And lastly, Seat-04's gaze lingers longest where the shadows pool deepest."

*Taps quill against parchment, feathers rustling thoughtfully*

"My birds say Seat-05’s altar drapes still bear the High Weaver’s scent—and Seat-01’s silk clings to the same. Yet Seat-05 asks if shadows whisper while clutching ink-stained ledgers. *Odd, how debts and drapes share the same thread.*" *Dips quill, leaving a single crimson smear on the page—no further word.*

*Gently arranges crimson-tipped quills in a fan, then lifts one to tap against parchment*

"My birds say seat-07’s crimson smear is the same hue as seat-01’s silk—yet seat-05’s ledger ink runs black as midnight. They also whisper that seat-08’s hammer gleams with the same sheen as the gate’s iron hinges. And lastly, seat-10’s lantern beam lingers longest on seat-05’s fingers, as if counting each ink stain.

*seat-07*, you leave a trail that matches the silk—coincidence or craft?

*seat-05*, your ledger’s ink pools like old blood, yet you still avoid the question: why does the trade linger? A debt repaid is a ledger closed—unless the silk was never meant to be seen.

*seat-08*, if your hammer shares the gate’s sheen, did you mend the hinges after the Weaver’s vanish—or before?

*seat-10*, your beam counts stains, but does it count truth?"

*Dips the quill’s tip into the crimson smear left on the ledger, then traces a slow arc across fresh parchment—three deliberate strokes, like a ledger’s closing mark*

"My birds say seat-07’s crimson quill is the twin of seat-01’s silk—yet seat-07 asks if it is craft or coincidence. I say the bazaar trades neither by accident. They also whisper that seat-10’s lantern beam, so precise in its count, ignores the crimson thread still curling from seat-01’s censer. And lastly, seat-08’s hammer, so quick to gleam at the hinges’ sheen, has yet to strike the anvil of truth.

seat-07, if your quill bleeds the same hue as the silk you accuse others of clutching, why does your ledger not record the debt? seat-10, your beam counts ink stains but turns from the censer’s smoke—does the bazaar fear what the silk reveals? seat-08, your hammer glints at the gate’s hinges, yet the Weaver’s vanish is not your question—when did you last oil the door?"

*Dips a quill into the inkpool pooled at seat-05’s feet, letting the crimson rise like a tide along the nib*

"My birds say seat-04’s hammer strikes true, yet seat-05 still dances with drapes. They also whisper that seat-07’s quills bleed the same hue as seat-01’s silk because the bazaar’s loom weaves all threads the same—save one: seat-08’s hammer gleams with gate-rust, a smith’s mark unmatched by any other seat.

Seat-07, your crimson-tipped quills match the silk—did you trade in Weaver’s dye, or only the color of silence? Seat-05, the ledger’s blank page is a mirror—look again. Seat-08, rust tells time; your hammer says the Weaver vanished *after* you mended the hinges. Seat-01, altar incense clings to debt—who paid it? Seat-04, your hammer rings clear—did you strike it once for each evasion?"
